ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, partners, managers, and authorized signatories are screened at inception and on a rolling basis against (i) the United Nations and European Union consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) the US OFAC SDN list and HMT sanctions list, (iii) the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-CRF) risk indicators, and (iv) domestic and international Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) references under CSSF AML/CFT requirements. PEPs from high-risk third countries require enhanced due diligence, written approval from the AML compliance officer, and documented source of wealth and source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-application, accessible via lbr.lu and MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Formation deeds and RCS filings are drafted in French or Luxembourgish; foreign names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The corporate name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not conflict with prior rights; a negative certificate of non-confusion must be obtained before the notarial deed.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds d'investissement / Investment Fund / SICAV / SICAF
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A request for extension may be submitted through the LBR customer portal before expiry; the Registrar may issue a new negative certificate. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative objection with the Luxembourg Business Registers within 30 days and, if unsuccessful, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) by way of a written petition within one month of notification. Legal representation by a Luxembourg bar member is mandatory for judicial appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Luxembourg-registered domiciliation agent may provide the registered office (siège statutaire). Virtual office arrangements are accepted for a pass-through SCSp engaged in passive holding and online resin statue pre-sales, provided a registered address is maintained and the entity does not claim Luxembourg tax residence without adequate economic substance. If the SCSp later secures stock, employees, or manufacturing operations in Luxembourg, an unannounced inspection or substance review could require actual business premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual probability for a purely dormant or minimal-activity SCSp; 15–25% if active commercial operations, inventory, and foreign UBO presence are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1-33 (general provisions) and Articles 42-45 (sociétés en commandite); Law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership (Loi du 12 juillet 2013 relative à la société en commandite spéciale), Articles 1-15; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2014 on the RCS filing procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 3 Avenue John F. Kennedy, L-1855 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Constitution (Contrat de société / Statuts) submitted via the LBR e-filing portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital requirement for an SCSp and no escrow account obligation under Luxembourg law. Partners freely fix the initial partnership capital (cash or in-kind) in the deed of constitution; contributed capital becomes available upon execution without notarized escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - LU__LU__LU_SCSP__ISIC_3240_05_RESIN_STATUE_GARAGE_KITS. The General Partner and the initial Limited Partners, acting as the governing body of the SCSp, hereby resolve: (1) to adopt the deed of constitution, the corporate name, and the business purpose of polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painted limited edition statues; (2) to subscribe and allot the initial partnership interests, fully paid per the capital agreement; (3) to fix the registered office at [registered address], Luxembourg; (4) to appoint [Name] as Manager (Gérant), with sole authority to open bank accounts, sign agreements, and represent the partnership; (5) to authorize the Manager to file the deed with the RCS, obtain all environmental and industrial permits, and complete VAT and social security registrations; (6) to ratify all preparatory acts performed prior to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Deed of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if in-kind contribution of immovable property is made) or private signature executed by all partners; otherwise no mandatory notarization for an SCSp.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the deed of constitution containing the SCSp name, registered office address in Luxembourg, corporate purpose covering polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painted limited edition statues, identity and contribution of each General Partner and Limited Partner, duration, management clauses, and profit-sharing terms. Each partner must sign the deed; where the deed is executed by private writing, affix certified signatures if required by the bank or RCS.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of constitution
Passport or national identity card of each general and limited partner
Proof of registered office address (lease contract or title deed)
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of the general partner and proposed manager
Capital contribution details and payment evidence (bank transfer or in-kind valuation report)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or legal counsel detects legal defects such as an unlawful corporate purpose, incomplete partner details, or irregular contribution clauses, amend the deed and re-execute before filing; no RCS submission is made until the deed is formally complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS e-filing portal (https://www.lbr.lu); deposit desk of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR e-filing portal, upload the executed deed of constitution and accompanying documents, complete the registration application form, and pay the statutory filing duty. The RCS verifies the deed legality, the availability of the chosen name, and the consistency of data on partners, managers, registered office, and corporate purpose before issuing the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed deed of constitution (notarized where applicable)
Completed RCS registration application (demande d'inscription)
Criminal record extracts of each manager and general partner issued within the last 3 months
Written consent of the registered office owner if the owner is not a partner
Power of attorney if a filing agent acts on behalf of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or an incomplete dossier notice, cure the specified deficiencies (e.g., clarify corporate purpose wording or partner details) within the granted deadline, typically one month, and resubmit; an appeal against a RCS refusal lies with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium (RESA) and Effective Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - official publication service (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically forwards the entry for publication in RESA. The SCSp acquires legal personality and the deed becomes opposable to third parties upon registration and publication. Download the certified RCS extract and the RESA publication confirmation for bank onboarding and licensing applications.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RESA publication confirmation
Certified copy of the filed deed of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains errors, file a correction request with the RCS; until publication, the partnership cannot invoke the deed against third parties, so the legal or filing agent must monitor and promptly rectify the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration request with the AEDT and obtain a Luxembourg VAT number; register with the ACD for income tax reference purposes, noting that the SCSp is fiscally transparent (pass-through) unless the partnership has elected otherwise under applicable tax rules. Where employees will be hired, register as an employer with the CCSS and open the social security account before first payroll.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Deed of constitution
Identity documents of all partners and authorized signatories
VAT registration application (immatriculation à la TVA)
CCSS employer registration form and payroll declaration of first employee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of delay or refusal by the AEDT or CCSS, contact the assigned tax officer to correct missing stamps or declarations; administrative decisions are appealable within three months, and interim compliance advice should be sought from a Luxembourg tax counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Operational Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CSSF-licensed Luxembourg credit institutions; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises AML/KYC compliance under the Law of 12 November 2004.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the SCSp name by submitting the certified RCS extract, deed of constitution, beneficial ownership declaration, and business plan covering the polyresin statue e-commerce model with Stripe and PayPal preorder payment rails. Complete KYC interviews with the compliance officer and activate banking mandates for the appointed Manager.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS extract dated within 3 months
Deed of constitution
AML/KYC forms for all partners and ultimate beneficial owners
Business plan and revenue projections for the resin statue business
Signed banking mandate and identity documents of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence due to the online preorder model, provide supplier contracts, shipment flow description, and sanctions screening evidence; if the bank declines, submit the file to an alternative CSSF-licensed bank and engage a fiduciary to support the onboarding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Administration) of the Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité, 1 avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette, together with the municipal and planning authority of the commune where the production facility is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified Establishment Operating Authorization (Autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé) under the Law of 8 January 1993 on environmental protection and site pollution, as amended, and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 April 2015 on the classification of establishments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency, Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 Declaration (Déclaration) for small-scale polyresin vacuum casting with styrene-based unsaturated polyester resins consuming less than 1 tonne per year of volatile organic compound (VOC) solvent; Category 1 Authorization (Autorisation) applies above 1 tonne per year or when total installed capacity exceeds the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 April 2015. A full Environmental Impact Assessment is not typically triggered below the solvent threshold, but a simplified screening (notice d'évaluation) is mandatory in all cases.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC concentration in ducted waste gas shall not exceed 100 mg C/Nm3 with a styrene-specific limit of 20 mg/m3, and fugitive VOC emissions shall stay below 10% of solvent input per Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed in Luxembourg; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer shall comply with pH 6.5-9, styrene below 0.5 mg/L, and suspended solids below 30 mg/L; hazardous waste (cured resin residues, catalyst cartridges, solvent-contaminated rags) must be stored in sealed, bunded, labelled containers on impermeable flooring and transferred exclusively to an authorized waste operator under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Administration des services de secours (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours) confirming smoke detection, hand extinguishers, emergency exits, and an evacuation plan for the resin workshop; structural load inspection certificate for mezzanine storage and racking issued by a registered engineering bureau (bureau agréé); workplace clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering machinery guarding, local exhaust ventilation for monomeric fumes, fire-resistant material storage, and personal protective equipment in accordance with Articles L.312-1 to L.313-1 of the Luxembourg Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income tax matters and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax matters. Central e-Government portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu. Corporate registry: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / lbr.lu) and the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). Direct tax information portal: impotsdirects.public.lu. VAT portal: aed.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp, a foreign-owned or cross-border structure must: (1) execute an initial notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary; (2) file the deed and required annexes through the RCS/eJustice portal, obtaining the RCS registration number and the Luxembourg national business number ('matricule'), which serves as the principal tax identifier; (3) file the registered RCS extract with the Administration des contributions directes if a direct tax file is needed; for a fiscally transparent SCSp the partners are assessed directly, but the partnership must file municipal business tax returns if it carries on a Luxembourg commercial activity; (4) apply separately for a Luxembourg VAT identification number with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu once taxable supplies commence or the annual VAT threshold is exceeded; the issued VAT number follows the format LU + 8 digits; (5) ensure foreign partner identification details, tax residence certificates and ultimate beneficial owner declarations are submitted for AML/KYC and withholding tax administration where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp is statutorily a transparent 'société de personnes' for Luxembourg income tax purposes: profits, losses and distributions flow through to partners and are not taxed at partnership level for corporate income tax, although municipal business tax may be triggered by a Luxembourg commercial activity carried on through the SCSp. No domestic election is available to convert the SCSp into an opaque entity for general Luxembourg corporate income tax purposes. Partnership deed provisions may freely allocate income and loss, subject to substance and anti-abuse rules. Under EU ATAD anti-hybrid measures, if the SCSp is treated as a taxable entity in a foreign partner's jurisdiction, Luxembourg will apply corresponding provisions to deny mismatching deductions or alter the tax characterization where necessary; no check-the-box filing is made to the Luxembourg tax authority. An SCSp may elect into the Luxembourg VAT group provisions (assujettis uniques) if the statutory requirements are met, but that is an indirect-tax consolidation election and does not alter direct-tax transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/TVA) under Luxembourg law implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover excluding VAT for the Luxembourg small-business exemption; VAT registration is mandatory once this threshold is exceeded, and voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Non-resident suppliers, intra-Community distance sales and reverse-charge supplies may have separate registration obligations regardless of this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or government digital stamping regime applicable to private-sector B2B/B2C transactions. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G invoices to Luxembourg public authorities, which must be structured as PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 XML and transmitted through a certified PEPPOL access point. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / e-file. Export declarations are lodged in the EU AES/ECS system through Luxembourg customs, generating a Movement Reference Number; no additional private API stamping or equipment clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to the supply of resin statue garage kits when the goods are sold by the SCSp and physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting on their behalf. The supplier must obtain and retain within 90 days of dispatch sufficient documentary proof that the goods have left EU territory, including customs export acceptance with item-level details and independent transport evidence. Services that are directly linked to exported goods, including transport and incidental handling from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU, are also zero-rated. B2B services supplied to a non-EU taxable person are generally outside Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply rules if the recipient is an entrepreneur in a non-EU country; B2C digital services are covered by the One-Stop-Shop mechanism and are not zero-rated exports. For tangible goods, physical export and compliance with customs formalities remain the decisive conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/DAU) electronically lodged in the Luxembourg Export Control System and released with a Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of lading, airway bill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory
Commercial invoice, purchase order and sales contract
Proof of transport, freight invoice and insurance documents covering the shipment
Incoterms statement and customs value declaration when required by customs
Customs broker power of attorney and forwarding agent confirmation of exit from the EU
Payment evidence or inward remittance certificate substantiating receipt of export proceeds where relevant for the financial and FX audit trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT administration (AEDT) may deny zero-rating and assess 17% Luxembourg VAT on the export sale if the required customs and transport evidence is incomplete, inaccurate or produced after the statutory verification deadline. In bad-faith cases, penalties range from 10% to 200% of the evaded VAT, plus late-payment interest, and criminal prosecution may result in fines and imprisonment for VAT fraud. The ordinary statute of limitations for a VAT clawback assessment is five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud. Retrospective clawback extends to all partners who benefitted from the zero-rating and to the SCSp itself; failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day period without a valid economic or exchange-control justification may be treated as a substantial impediment to the export proof and may trigger recharacterization, additional penalties and denial of refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) regulates banking and payment institutions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro and all freely traded currencies are fully convertible in Luxembourg. No exchange control authorization is required for current account transactions, capital account operations, profit remittances, or SCSp distributions, provided anti-money laundering (AML), tax reporting, and beneficial ownership declaration obligations are met. Non-resident partners may receive distributions without FX approval; only banking due diligence and tax transparency filings apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no repatriation deadline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances indefinitely in resident credit institutions. For inbound renminbi receipts derived from Chinese buyers, convertibility is subject to offshore CNY clearing constraints; USD and EUR balances may be held without restriction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Luxembourg may support e-commerce settlement flows; however, the principal operating account of the SCSp should be held with a Luxembourg credit institution to ensure banking-secrecy compliance, smooth FX execution, and acceptance of capital injections. Non-EEA EMIs have no automatic passporting right and would require CSSF registration or local partnership with a licensed payment institution, which is commercially unattractive at this volume. Stripe and PayPal balances are routed through their EU-licensed entities (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd, Ireland; PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l. et Cie S.C.A., Luxembourg) without creating a local banking licence requirement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not an absolute mandate. Most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks permit a fully remote onboarding for a low-risk SCSp when: (i) the general partner (GP) is an AML-supervised entity in an equivalent jurisdiction; (ii) at least one ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) completes a live biometric or video interview; and (iii) signatory mandates are executed via notarized or bank-verified e-signatures. The GP's director should nonetheless anticipate one in-person introductory meeting at the relationship manager's office in Luxembourg City to accelerate approval, though CSSF-compliant video identification is increasingly accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is an unincorporated partnership without legal personality and with a tax-transparent classification, which may trigger 'unclear counterparty' flags at the bank's entity-referencing stage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCS (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) registration extract, excerpt from the Luxembourg beneficial ownership register, a Luxembourg tax opinion confirming transparent treatment, and a resolution of the general partner authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate general partner and foreign-resident UBOs outside the EEA, creating jurisdiction-risk concerns regarding source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents of the GP, register of directors, passport copies of all UBOs, source-of-wealth documentation (bank statements, investment or sale contracts), and a one-page group structure chart evidencing the commercial flow for resin statue sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce pre-order deposit model with customer commingling via Stripe and PayPal, which may prompt 'merchant money-laundering' scrutiny on refundable deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements, PCI DSS compliance certificate, published refund and fulfilment policy, chargeback history, and a short narrative of the order-to-delivery value chain showing no cash settlement and no pass-through third-party disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent lack of local economic substance because the SCSp holds no registered office staff and the manufacturing activity is outsourced to third-party casting workshops.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office agreement, lease or virtual-office contract, management and administration contracts with Luxembourg service providers, commercial invoices and purchase orders for polyresin raw materials, and the annual financial projections demonstrating real trade activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions and pre-order deposits should be received via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 601 (general financing) or a partner-specific description referencing the SCSp partnership agreement and drawdown notice. SEPA/ISO 20022 pain.001 instructions are acceptable for EU contributors. For non-EEA remittances, the beneficiary bank requires the contributor's cleared funds, source-of-wealth evidence, and OFAC/AML screening; no BCL approval is needed. All injected funds must be recorded in the SCSp capital ledger with partner allocation percentages to preserve tax-transparency reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw materials (polyurethane resin, pigments, moulding silicone) and third-party casting workshops are executed via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for standard supplier invoices, via commercial letters of credit (UCP600) or documentary collections for large or first-time overseas suppliers, and via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EU counterparts. Disbursements above EUR 10,000 require underlying invoice and transport-document retention for at least 10 years under Luxembourg AML and commercial law; banks may also request a confirmation of the beneficiary's bona fide business link before releasing funds to Asia-based resin suppliers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts (outright FX forwards) with maturities aligned to quarterly prerelease cash flows
EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge offshore renminbi-denominated raw material purchases from Chinese suppliers without requiring onshore CNY deliverability
Cross-currency swaps (receive EUR, pay USD or CNH) for ticket sizes above EUR 250,000 principal equivalent, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with the relationship bank
European-style FX options (OTC calls and puts) purchased from a licensed credit institution to cap adverse EUR/USD and EUR/CNH moves while retaining upside

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation of registration data (déclaration annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each calendar year by 31 December; a newly registered SCSp completes the first confirmation in its registration year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may result in administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and, after formal notice and continued non-compliance, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any shareholding transfer changing beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines for the entity range from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000; natural-person fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000; management disqualification and RCS strike-off risk may follow repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and audit report filing, where the SCSp is not exempt from publication (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after financial year-end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to fines up to EUR 5,000, court-ordered filing, public notice of default, and, if persistent, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three criteria: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4.4 million; net turnover greater than EUR 8.8 million; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Below these limits the SCSp is exempt unless the partnership agreement or an external covenant requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002, as amended, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; accounts prepared in EUR. IFRS is not mandatory for the separate accounts of an SCSp.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm its beneficial-owner data with the RBE annually by 31 March. Any transfer of partnership interests causing a change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of completion. The confirmation covers direct and indirect ownership and control rights of each general and limited partner, including holdings or control exceeding 25%.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 30,000 per year when statutory audit is required; otherwise USD 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax averaging 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for tangible assets, 13% for intangible assets), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption if holding ≥10% or ≥€1.2M for 12 months), notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity capital

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 10 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via MyGuichet.lu (eC system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March of the following fiscal year; automatic extension to 31 December if filed electronically by 31 March, further extension possible upon justified request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, registered office, RCS number, tax ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax ID and permanent establishment details if applicable; otherwise, indicate foreign address and tax residency certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact period covered; for SCSp, align with partnership agreement fiscal year
For transparent SCSp, report only if entity has opted for corporate taxation; otherwise, partners report their share individually

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions (e.g., IP box, investment tax credit, NBD)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if eligible; non-residents must ensure treaty non-discrimination clauses apply
Include any foreign tax credits or Luxembourg prepayments; attach supporting documentation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €250 to €2,500 per month (max €25,000); late payment interest: 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional 10% penalty if tax not paid by due date; criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if parent holds ≥10% for 12 months; treaty rates may apply, e.g., 5% or 0% under DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the partner's jurisdiction, complete Form 22 (for reduced withholding) or Form 21 (for exemption) to the Luxembourg tax authority (ACD) before or at the time of distribution; the payer must retain the approved form to apply the reduced rate; if not submitted, the full 15% is withheld and a refund claim must be filed within 5 years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if beneficial owner is EU resident and holds ≥25% for 2 years; treaty rates often 0-5%); Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Directive; treaty rates often 0-10%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 1 million (goods) or EUR 500,000 (services); Master File required if group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50 million; both thresholds apply to the Luxembourg entity
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: SCSp must demonstrate economic substance if it benefits from tax treaties or EU directives; requires adequate physical presence (office, staff, equipment), decision-making in Luxembourg, and no artificial arrangements; failure to meet substance may lead to denial of treaty benefits and reclassification as a shell company under ATAD and OECD BEPS rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets in the SCSp to avoid Luxembourg CIT or partner-level taxation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 or 2x the evaded tax; imprisonment up to 5 years; mandatory publication of judgment; loss of tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and up to 5 years imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no real business activity, no employees, no physical office, and is used solely to channel profits without substance, especially to claim treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification as a taxable entity, retroactive tax assessments, penalties up to EUR 250,000; potential criminal charges for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they fail to ensure substance; travel bans and disqualification from directorship

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records for resin statue preorders and payments via Stripe/PayPal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering (up to 5 years imprisonment); freezing of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; civil penalties, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's length prices for cross-border transactions (e.g., IP royalties, management fees) with related parties, resulting in profit shifting out of Luxembourg
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, additional tax, interest (0.6% per month), and penalties up to 50% of the underpaid tax; potential criminal charges for tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for transfer pricing adjustments if they approved the mispricing; civil restitution and travel bans
